title: Migraine: where acute and preventive drugs act
ariaLabel: Schematic of a migraine attack: trigeminal nerve endings release CGRP, which widens meningeal vessels and causes neurogenic inflammation, and pain signals are amplified in the brainstem. Triptans act on 5-HT1B and 1D receptors to constrict vessels and reduce CGRP release, CGRP antagonists and antibodies block CGRP, and NSAIDs lower pain signalling.
caption: Schematic, not to scale. Flow and levels are qualitative and illustrative; no dose, concentration or lipid value is shown or implied.
blockInfo: A drug of the chosen class acting at this step (generic teaching symbol, not a named drug's shape). Less passes here, with the effects shown at the cholesterol and the LDL receptors.

edges.label: CGRP signalling
edges.info: CGRP antagonists (gepants) and CGRP antibodies block CGRP or its receptor. Triptans also lower its release through 5-HT1D receptors.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: 5-HT1B receptors
edges.info: Triptans act on 5-HT1B receptors of vessels and constrict them. They are contraindicated in coronary disease because of this effect.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: pain amplification
edges.info: NSAIDs lower prostaglandin-driven sensitisation of pain pathways. Antiemetics help nausea and speed absorption.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

sources: Where each class acts. Triptans act on 5-HT1B and 1D receptors, CGRP antagonists and antibodies block CGRP, and NSAIDs lower pain signalling. This is standard teaching in the pharmacology texts the PrepNucleus lessons cite (Katzung; KD Tripathi) and were not checked against a linked source here, so they are flagged for review.
simplified: Ergotamine, antiemetics, preventive drugs (propranolol, topiramate, amitriptyline), aura, medication-overuse headache, other headaches, cardiovascular contraindications and adverse effects are left out. Migraine pain is drawn as a teaching score. Levels and the size of each effect are illustrative. The drug choices are teaching toggles of a class: no named drug, dose or schedule is shown or implied, and the figure does not say who should or should not take any of them.
